selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Who is being talked about in this passage as moving through the world and sky?
questions.answer: A traveler who is learning about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What number of truths is summarized here?
questions.answer: Five truths.

questions.question: What is the faith statement repeated before the long list of proofs?
questions.answer: That there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s greatness and majesty?
questions.answer: They are complete and cover everything.

questions.question: What keeps those deeds from being wild or messy?
questions.answer: Allah’s will and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how things in creation fit together?
questions.answer: They are together, linked, and connected.

questions.question: Why does the universal order show that partners cannot be with Allah?
questions.answer: Because one great order fits one Maker, not many.

questions.question: What can a child infer from everything being connected so well?
questions.answer: One Lord planned it all together.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the things spread all over the earth?
questions.answer: Their unity shows they belong to one Maker.

questions.question: What does the Arabic line at the end mean in a simple way?
questions.answer: Everything has a sign that points to Allah being One.

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: Many signs in creation show Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the traveler see in the world that helps him believe this?
questions.answer: Many proofs and signs in creation.

questions.question: What is the most important statement in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah is the only true God.

questions.question: When the passage speaks about greatness and fullness, what is it helping prove?
questions.answer: Allah’s necessary existence and unity.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the making of creatures?
questions.answer: They are made quickly, easily, and in huge numbers.

questions.question: What does “excellent design and value” teach about creation?
questions.answer: It is carefully made and precious.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the order found all around creation?
questions.answer: It is general and does not fit the idea of many gods.

questions.question: What do Allah’s Names and deeds do in the universe?
questions.answer: They reach everywhere together.

questions.question: What do the Names, deeds, elements, and species all have in common in this passage?
questions.answer: They all act as proofs of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Who is noticing the truths in this passage?
questions.answer: A voyager who is observing the universe.

questions.question: Who learns these lessons in the passage?
questions.answer: A traveler passing through the cosmos.

questions.question: What do these truths point to about Allah?
questions.answer: They show that Allah is One and Unique.

questions.question: How far do Allah’s deeds reach, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They reach without limit.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect idea is in the part about many creatures being made well?
questions.answer: Since so many are made so perfectly and easily, one all-powerful Creator must be doing it.
